---
title: "For educators"
description: >-
  Instructor packs for published lessons, the licence that lets you reuse them,
  how to cite the project, and how to suggest improvements.
---

An instructor pack is a Markdown file with a lecturer guide, the learning
objectives and prerequisites of the lesson, the approximate time, a student
assignment, a rubric, a reference solution that the build runs, accessibility
notes, and a way to teach the lesson without an AI tool. You do not need to
register or to contact anyone to use one.

## Packs

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pathlib import Path

from pbc.authoring import LearningPath
from pbc.authoring.educators import packs_list
from pbc.authoring.website import project_root

print(packs_list(LearningPath.read(project_root(Path.cwd()))))
```

The objectives, prerequisites, and difficulty in a pack are written from the
front matter of its lesson, so they match the lesson on this site.

## Reuse

Lesson text, figures, and the packs are under
[CC BY 4.0](https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction/blob/main/LICENSE-CONTENT):
you may adapt them, including commercially, when you give credit, link to the
licence, and indicate changes. Code is under the
[MIT licence](https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction/blob/main/LICENSE).

## Cite

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pbc.authoring.educators import citation_text

print(f"> {citation_text()}")
```

The text is built from `CITATION.cff`, which GitHub reads to offer "Cite this
repository". The project has no DOI.

## Suggest an improvement

Open an issue from one of the forms. The outcome is recorded on the issue; no
form asks for contact details.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pbc.authoring.educators import forms_list

print(forms_list())
```
